subject: Final MSA redlines + private-hosting attestation timeline
messages:
From: Ellis Rangel <ellis.rangel@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Cardinal Health Legal <legal@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Final MSA redlines + private-hosting attestation timeline

Mateo —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached are our consolidated MSA redlines for the Private Hosting addenda (Cardinal_Health_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). A few high-level items we need to close:

- Confirmation of license scope for on-prem/VPC: Cardinal requires explicit language that runtime copies used for private hosting remain subject to customer-controlled backups and that no derivatives will be rehosted by Redwood outside the agreed boundary.
- Operator access / audit window: we propose a 48-hour on-demand audit window and retain the right to require witness certification for any snapshot transfers.
- Evidence and escrow-like deposit: we would prefer an encrypted sealed snapshot deposit with third-party auditor attestation versus manual custody handoff.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the three items above and provide the latest attestation template you plan to use? We have procurement & security legal aligned internally and are targeting signature + PO by Feb 26.

I attached the redlines and a draft Order Form (OrderForm-Cardinal-PrivDeploy.xlsx). Please let me know if you need a short call with our security team (Sung Park) next week.

Thanks,
Ellis Rangel
Director, Cloud Integrations
Cardinal Health

Attachments: Cardinal_Health_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx, OrderForm-Cardinal-PrivDeploy.xlsx
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Rangel <ellis.rangel@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final MSA redlines + private-hosting attestation timeline

Ellis —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. I attached a one-page executive summary and our working attestation template (RD-8342-privdeploy-exec-summary.pdf). High level response to your bullets: 

- License scope: we can add explicit language that runtime instances deployed to customer-controlled VPCs/on-prem remain subject to the deployment boundary and that Redwood will not host derived customer models outside the agreed environment. We'll propose a clause and share redline by EOD tomorrow.
- Operator access / audit window: we typically limit operator access to scheduled maintenance and emergency access with strict logging. 48 hours on-demand is reasonable if we couple it with a signed witnessing plan; Laura (legal) has a suggested alternative below.
- Escrow-like deposit: we prefer an encrypted sealed snapshot deposit with attestation by an independent auditor. We've attached our attestation template for your legal review (Redwood_Attestation_Template.docx) and a short runbook. If Cardinal agrees, we can include an exhibit describing transfer mechanics.

We can do a short alignment call with Sung — I'm available Mon/Tue next week after 10am PT. Laura / Neha, can you weigh in on the proposed redline approach? Ellis, I'll circulate the DocuSign link once we confirm the final Order Form.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RD-8342-privdeploy-exec-summary.pdf, Redwood_Attestation_Template.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Rangel <ellis.rangel@cardinalhealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final MSA redlines + private-hosting attestation timeline

Ellis / team —

Thanks for sending the consolidated redlines. I reviewed the MSA addendum and the Order Form. A few legal points and suggested language to avoid scope creep: 

1) License / derivative hosting: replace broad prohibition with specific deployment boundary language. Proposed sentence: "Redwood shall not host, deploy, or distribute Customer Models or any Derivative Works of Customer Models outside the Customer Deployment Boundary specified in Exhibit A without Customer's prior written consent." This keeps the protection you want while enabling necessary support variants.

2) Operator access and audit windows: we cannot agree to an unrestricted 48-hour on-demand access right. Suggested compromise: 48-hour audit window that must be scheduled with 72 hours' notice, except in documented emergencies where Redwood may request time-limited access (max 8 hours) subject to Customer approval and accompanied by an independent witness or auditor. Add logging, session recording, and a post-access attestation.

3) Escrow-like snapshot deposit: we support the encrypted sealed snapshot approach. Key requirements: (a) snapshot stored encrypted under a customer-owned KMS key; (b) transfer via mutually agreed escrow agent or API endpoint; (c) notarized attestation from an independent auditor confirming integrity and chain-of-custody. We suggest referencing the attestation template (attached) as Exhibit B.

Next steps from Redwood legal: I will prepare a tracked-change MSA addendum that incorporates the Exhibit A boundary language and the attestation exhibit. Mateo — can you push the updated addendum into the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign envelope once Cardinal confirms acceptance? Ellis — if Cardinal's legal accepts the attestation flow we should be able to close the Order Form without additional procurement gating.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Attestation_Template.docx
From: Ellis Rangel <ellis.rangel@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Cardinal Health Legal <legal@cardinalhealth.com>, Sung Park <sung.park@cloudops.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final MSA redlines + private-hosting attestation timeline

Mateo / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language, Laura. Cardinal legal is comfortable with the deployment-boundary sentence you proposed, and the escrow/attestation approach looks acceptable pending one small edit to require auditor independence by contract (we'll add a short definition).

On operator access we can accept the scheduled 72-hours notice flow with an explicit emergency carveout (8-hour time-limited access) — we'll mark that in our follow-up redline and expect the session recording + post-access attestation.

Procurement update: we will route the Order Form to our purchasing team today. Target for signature + PO is Feb 26. Please go ahead and load your tracked MSA addendum and the attestation exhibit to the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8342) and share the DocuSign link when ready.

Also attaching a short runbook our ops team would like included as an appendix — I will send that as a separate file momentarily. If we can get the DocuSign envelope out by early next week we should be on track.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Ellis Rangel
Director, Cloud Integrations
Cardinal Health
